content:
Requirement R17 (input): Command Track Target of Interest (TOI). Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to command tracking of a target of interest..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-17.1, F-17.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-17.<F>.1, Be-17.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-17.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R17 lets the pilot command the UAV to track a designated target of interest (TOI) — i.e. issue the tracking order once a target is identified.

**Function candidates:**

- **F-17.1 — Designate the TOI:** the goal of establishing *which* target the UAV should track (spatial/identity selection of the target). Effect: a target is unambiguously specified.

- **F-17.2 — Command the UAV to track the designated TOI:** the goal of committing the tracking order — directing UAV sensors to lock/center on the specified target. Effect: UAV enters tracking on that target.

- **F-17.3 — Confirm tracking order execution:** the goal of making the pilot aware the UAV has acknowledged and is tracking. Effect: pilot knows tracking is active.

**Recommendation:** Close on **F-17.2** as the primary Function for R17. Rationale:
- F-17.3 is acknowledgment/notification — already covered by the shared R08 notification stack (steps 7.1.7–7.1.10 map directly to it). No new Function needed here.
- F-17.1 (designation) heavily overlaps R14 (aim ISR sensor at a target via press-hold/option-ring designation). Reusing R14's designation surface for target selection is the sensible move rather than re-deriving a designation Function. Flag: **F-17.1 designation should be treated as shared with R14, not owned by R17.**

So R17's genuinely new intent is the *tracking command* itself — F-17.2.

Which do you want to close on?

Both closed as Functions for R17:

- **F-17.1 — Designate the TOI** (shared designation goal, reuses R14's target-selection surface)
- **F-17.2 — Command the UAV to track the designated TOI** (commit the tracking order)

Note carried forward: F-17.3 (execution confirmation) folds into the shared R08 notification stack — not a standalone Function here.

Moving to **Behaviour**. I'll cover both closed Functions.

---

**For F-17.1 (Designate the TOI):**

- **Be-17.1.1 — Touch-only:** pilot taps a target symbol on the Map/ISR feed to select it; press-hold on empty space drops a TOI marker at that point. Reuses R14 press-hold → option-ring designation pattern. Selected target highlights as the active TOI.

- **Be-17.1.2 — Keyboard-only:** pilot cycles through detected tracks/contacts with a bezel rotary (step through target list), OSS to confirm selection; or enters target coordinates/track-ID via UCP alphanumeric.

**For F-17.2 (Command tracking):**

- **Be-17.2.1 — Touch-only:** with a TOI active, pilot selects "TRACK" from the option-ring (or a dedicated on-screen TRACK button) → one-shot commit sends the order.

- **Be-17.2.2 — Keyboard-only:** dedicated bezel TRACK OSS → press to commit tracking on the active TOI.

- **Be-17.2.3 — Mixed:** designate via Touch (tap target), commit via Keyboard (bezel TRACK OSS) — adds value because designation is spatial (better by touch) while commit is a discrete safety-relevant action (better by a fixed physical button, glove/vibration-tolerant).

---

**Recommendation:** The Mixed pathway (Be-17.2.3) genuinely earns its place — spatial designation and discrete commit have different ergonomic optima in this cockpit. But note both sub-behaviours must stay modality-complete (each modality alone must complete designate+commit), so Mixed is an *offered convenience*, not a required split.

Want me to keep all these, or narrow?

All Behaviours closed:

**F-17.1 (Designate TOI):**
- Be-17.1.1 — Touch-only (tap target / press-hold marker, reuses R14 pattern)
- Be-17.1.2 — Keyboard-only (bezel rotary track-cycle + OSS confirm, or UCP coord/ID entry)

**F-17.2 (Command tracking):**
- Be-17.2.1 — Touch-only (option-ring/on-screen TRACK → one-shot commit)
- Be-17.2.2 — Keyboard-only (bezel TRACK OSS commit)
- Be-17.2.3 — Mixed (Touch designate + Keyboard commit)

Constraint carried: each modality alone stays modality-complete; Mixed is convenience, not a locked split.

---

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI element sets, mapping to the closed Be indices.

**S-17.1.1.1 — Map/ISR-anchored designation surface (serves Be-17.1.1, Be-17.1.2):**
- Reuse **Map view** + **R16 ISR Feed Panel** as the target-selection canvas.
- **Track/contact glyph layer** (reused/extended from R05 marker layer) — tappable target symbols; selected TOI highlights.
- **Press-hold → option-ring** (shared R05/R14 pattern) for marker drop / designation on empty space.
- **Bezel rotary** = step through track list; **bezel OSS** = confirm selection (Keyboard path).
- **UCP alphanumeric** = enter track-ID / coordinates (Keyboard path).
- **TDC** available for cursor-mediated target pointing on WAD (HOTAS-resident, hands-on-throttle).

**S-17.2.1.1 — Tracking commit controls (serves Be-17.2.1/.2/.3):**
- **Option-ring "TRACK" segment** (Touch, appears on active TOI — reuses R14 ring).
- **Dedicated bezel TRACK OSS** (Keyboard commit).
- **TOI detail/status row** with inline TRACK affordance (reuses R12/R13 Detail Panel chassis) — surfaces active-TOI state and a commit control.

**S-17.x — Acknowledgment:** reuse **shared R08 notification stack** (audio tone + visual pop-up/marker) for the 7.1.7–7.1.10 execution confirmation. No new element.

---

**Reuse flags (heavy):** almost everything here is shared — Map/glyph layer (R05), option-ring (R14), Detail Panel (R12/R13), ISR Feed Panel (R16), Setpoint isn't needed (that's R18/distance), notification stack (R08). R17's *only* genuinely new element is the **TRACK commit affordance** (option-ring segment + bezel OSS + detail-panel row), which is a thin addition to existing surfaces.

Want all three structure sets, or consolidate?

All Structures closed:

**F-17.1 (Designate TOI):**
- **S-17.1.1.1** — Map/ISR-anchored designation surface: Map view + R16 ISR Feed Panel canvas, reused track/contact glyph layer, press-hold→option-ring (R05/R14), bezel rotary track-cycle + OSS confirm, UCP track-ID/coord entry, TDC cursor pointing. Serves Be-17.1.1 + Be-17.1.2.

**F-17.2 (Command tracking):**
- **S-17.2.1.1** — Tracking commit controls: option-ring TRACK segment (Touch), dedicated bezel TRACK OSS (Keyboard), TOI detail-panel row with inline TRACK affordance (R12/R13 chassis). Serves Be-17.2.1/.2/.3.

**Shared (acknowledgment):**
- R08 notification stack (audio tone + visual pop-up/marker) for execution confirmation. No new element.

**Net-new to R17:** only the TRACK commit affordance (ring segment + bezel OSS + detail row). Everything else reused.

---

R17 fully drafted across all three layers:
- **Functions:** F-17.1 (designate TOI), F-17.2 (command tracking)
- **Behaviours:** Be-17.1.1/.1.2 (designate), Be-17.2.1/.2.2/.2.3 (commit)
- **Structures:** S-17.1.1.1 (designation surface), S-17.2.1.1 (commit controls)

Ready for you to close R17, or revisit any layer.
